title: 5.4.6 Lab: Pipes that come and go
description: The starter builds one pair of pipes and leaves it. Build a new pair on a timer, keep them in an array, and delete the ones that have left the screen.

steps.title: Build a pair on a timer
steps.instructions: The function `makePipe()` is given: it builds one pair and returns the top pipe. In `draw()`, call it every 90 frames and put the result in the `pipes` array. Run it: pipes should keep arriving from the right. The bird can touch a pipe and nothing happens yet; 5.4.8 makes that end the round.

steps.title: Delete the pipes that have gone
steps.instructions: Loop over `pipes` from the end to the start. When a pipe's `x` is less than -30, delete its `mate` and the pipe itself, and splice it out of the array.
hints: `for (let i = pipes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { ... }` is the backwards loop from 5.4.5.

steps.title: Show how many are alive
steps.instructions: Draw `pipes.length` on the screen, inside `drawTop()` at the bottom of the starter, so no pipe can cover it. It should rise to two or three and then hold there. If it keeps climbing, pipes are not being removed.
hints: `text('pipes: ' + pipes.length, 20, 50);` goes inside `drawTop()`, under the 'tap space to flap' line.

requirements.title: A pair is built on a repeating beat
requirements.description: A remainder test on the frame count builds a pair at a steady rate. Help: 5.4.5 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: Every pair goes into the array
requirements.description: The pair is built and pushed inside the beat's if, so a pair arrives once per beat, not every frame. Help: 5.4.5 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: Pipes that have left are deleted and spliced out
requirements.description: Inside an if that tests a pipe's x (off the left edge), the sprite is deleted and also taken out of the array. Help: 5.4.5 (Reading: A world that scrolls)
